subject: Clarify billing for streaming partial outputs & disconnect retries
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@datawave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Billing for streaming: partial outputs / disconnects — need clarity

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. As we prep procurement docs for our pilot, finance has a couple of specific questions about how Redwood bills streaming responses. Two concrete scenarios they want spelled out so we can land language in the SOW: 

1) Partial generation + client disconnect: if a streaming response generates 600 tokens and the client disconnects after receiving 210 tokens, does DataWave get billed for 600 tokens or 210?

2) Retries / reconnects: if our client automatically retries the same request (same prompt) after a disconnect and the model re-sends the rest of the content, will we be charged twice for tokens that were re-generated?

Also: what protections does Redwood have to avoid double-billing in common mobile/connectivity-flaky cases? We are under tight cost constraints and procurement asked about explicit guarantees or contract language around duplicate charges from retries.

Can you provide a plain-language explanation and an example invoice line or sample math that we can pass to procurement? If there are configurable headers or client-side knobs that avoid re-generation, please list those too — we can change the client if needed.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
DataWave Analytics

Subject: Re: Billing for streaming: partial outputs / disconnects — need clarity

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear scenarios. I’ll summarize the commercial position and loop in engineering (Marissa) for the exact runtime behavior and headers we recommend. High-level answers first, then we’ll follow with a technical note and sample invoice math.

High-level (commercial):
- Billing basis: tokens that the Redwood runtime generates are billable. In practice this generally aligns with tokens emitted on the stream, but there are edge cases below.
- Partial disconnects: tokens that were already generated by the model are billable even if the client didn’t receive them. In your example, if the runtime generated 600 tokens and the client only got 210 before disconnect, the billable amount is up to 600 tokens.
- Retries: we have de-duplication and resume mechanisms (see technical note) that prevent double-billing in common retry cases if the client follows best practices (reuse the same request id / resume header). If retries cause the model to re-generate the same tokens on the server-side, those regenerated tokens are billable.
- Discounts / committed usage: committed discounts apply to billable tokens (including tokens generated as part of retries). For larger customers we can carve out contractual credits for systemic replay events (e.g., provider-level incident causing replay across many requests). We generally treat client-local flaky networks as customer responsibility, but we’ll include a reasonable exception clause for large-scale replay incidents.

Attachments: I’ve attached the latest streaming rate card and a tiny example invoice showing token math for your two scenarios (redwood_streaming_ratecard_v2.pdf, example_invoice_diff.xlsx).

Next steps I propose: 1) Marissa will confirm exact headers and timing windows; 2) If you’d like, Vanessa and I can propose SOW language that specifies the de-duplication window and the exception threshold for credits; 3) quick 30-min call tomorrow to finalize.

Marissa — can you add the precise runtime behavior (dedupe window, cache retention, recommended headers) inline here?

Best,

Hi Aisha — quick technical dive and explicit examples. I pasted the short TL;DR at the top, then the details.

TL;DR
- Billing is charged for tokens the runtime generates (tokenization + decode step) — not on client ACK.
- If you retry within the client-side dedup window with the same X-Request-ID, we will attempt to resume from the KV cache and avoid re-generating tokens (no duplicate charge). Default dedupe window: 15 seconds.
- KV cache retention for streaming resume: 30 seconds by default. Outside these windows a retry will re-generate tokens and be billed again.

Concrete examples (to match Aisha’s scenarios):
1) Partial generation + client disconnect
- Request A generates N=600 tokens on the runtime. Client receives 210 and disconnects. Runtime has already produced all 600 tokens; therefore invoice shows 600 billable tokens for that request. (The deliverability to client does not change the generated-token charge.)

2) Retry within dedupe window (no double-billing)
- Client includes header X-Request-ID: 123e4567 and retries the same request within 15 seconds. Runtime finds a match in the stream dedupe cache and returns from the cached sequence (or resumes the stream) without re-running autoregressive generation for already-produced tokens -> single billable generation.

3) Retry outside dedupe window (double-billing possible)
- Same request but retried after 45s. Cache TTL has expired (30s). Runtime will re-execute generation and the newly generated tokens are billable; invoice will reflect both runs.

Practical recommendations to avoid accidental double charges:
- Use X-Request-ID: client-generated UUID for each logical request. Keep it stable across retries.
- Use X-Resume-Stream: true when attempting to reconnect; Redwood will attempt to reattach to the cached stream before regenerating.
- Emit a finalization call (/streams/commit) once the client successfully completes the response — this helps us close the cache and mark the request as complete on our side.
- Monitor the streaming-cost-metrics endpoint (we can enable per-route token emission metrics for your account) and set a per-request cost cap header (X-Cost-Cap-Tokens) to avoid runaway partials during testing.

Operational notes for procurement language:
- We recommend SOW text that says: “Redwood bills tokens generated by the runtime. Retries with the same X-Request-ID within a 15s deduplication window are not billed twice; repeats outside the window may be billed twice. For provider incidents that cause systemic replays, Redwood will evaluate credits for token recharges above 1,000,000 tokens/day.” We can adjust thresholds during contracting.

Limitations / model variant notes:
- Older model variants in our catalog (v1.0–v1.2) do not support stream resume; they will re-run generation on retry even if the same request id is supplied. Newer variants (v2.x and our Redwood-verified streaming models) support resume/dedupe. We’ll include a model-compatibility matrix in the SOW.

If you’d like, I can produce a short one-paragraph statement for procurement that you can paste into the contract.
